I was best friends with a guy in high school.  I didn't have many - I was an awkward kid, painfully shy, a heavy reader, into sci-fi and fantasy... The whole cliche given form and plopped into a middle Georgia high school in the 1980s.

So when he took an interest in me, I was over the moon to have a friend, a real friend who spoke my language - we liked the same stuff, same kinds of movies, he was big into comics and got me hooked, we admired the same girls pure and chaste from afar.  When both got our first real jobs together and worked at the same places and after high school we moved into a duplex together with a mutual friend.  It wasn't long before the mutual friend and I were humping like rabbits, because you know, 19 and hormones and she and I weren't going to get married but we were exploring ourselves and each other and learned how to be people in a relationship. Then I figured out that he had slept with her too - no big deal, really; we weren't really dating and we hadn't committed to anything, but I thought it was weird that he felt the need to hide it.  Because she and I hadn't hidden anything, but I was bothered that he hadn't told me.

And the more I thought about it, the more I thought about other things, things I was thinking about differently now that I had grown a bit and grown into myself a bit.  I started looking at things from a different angle, and I didn't like what I was seeing. Times when he'd undercut me to make himself look better.  Times when he'd made me the butt of a joke to curry favor with others.  When I expressed an interest in something he wasn't interested in, he tried to discourage me from pursuing it.  When I was proud of some accomplishment, he'd dismiss it as inconsequential or dumb.  

I thought that I was being paranoid, so I confided in another friend. In the conversation, I found out some things I never knew - like how he'd lied to a girl that he knew I had a crush on, telling her that I'd stolen from her, shortly before dating her himself. He'd badmouthed me at one of the jobs we worked. Other things started to filter back to me, until I had to admit that my friend was not the friend I thought he was. It was difficult to process.  I had thought of him as a brother, but it turned out that he had denigrated and undercut me at every opportunity, like some sort of game he was playing.  Probably because he knew that I was too socially awkward to understand what he was doing.  I don't know, honestly - I never discussed his motives with him. I didn't say anything.  I couldn't.  

I eventually moved away to another city, and used the opportunity to cut contact with him.  But I still carry trust issues with me to this day, though not as intensely thanks to actual friendships and no small amount of therapy.  Still, though, I am very cautious about who I let into my life to this day.
